title: tile-aware quantization + dimension fixups for Llama/Mistral/Qwen runtime quirks
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Model-specific tiling + quantization fixes: improves throughput and p95 latency for Llama/Mistral/Qwen on mixed-sequence workloads. Removes a small KV-cache eviction bug causing stale prefixes for some MQA paths.
description:
Context & motivation: We observed repeated regressions on short prompt p95 latency and MQA memory spikes in production traces for multiple customers using Llama-2 and Qwen models. Investigation showed three separate but interacting issues: (1) tile/quant alignment mismatch for MQA/GQA quantized kernels producing suboptimal vectorized code paths, (2) per-model dimension/rotary handling differences (Mistral's chunked rotary vs Llama's contiguous rotary) triggering inefficient kernel selection, and (3) a KV-cache prefix eviction heuristic that could evict entries prematurely for continuous-batching workloads.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds tile-aware quantization padding and kernel selection heuristics, introduces small per-model dimension fixups for rotary and layernorm edge-cases, and tightens the KV-cache retention policy for continuous batching. Also includes microbenchmarks, unit tests, and documentation.

Key changes (high-level):
- kernel_selector.cc: new tile-aware scoring function that factors quant tile size, vector width and model shape priors; forces 16-byte alignment for kernels with quantized inner loops to avoid scalar fallbacks.
- tiling_helpers.cc and qwen_fixes.h: add safe-padding helpers that insert a zero-pad codepath only when needed by the backend, avoiding blanket buffer copies.
- llama_runner.cc & mistral_adapter.cc: per-model adapters that normalize rotary chunking and restore expected KV-length semantics; small branch that forces the GQA path for known MQA shapes when quant packing was previously ambiguous.
- kv_cache_manager.cc: adjust prefix eviction: prefer least-recent-seen-complete-request instead of simple time-based churn; prevents eviction during steady continuous-batching traffic with many short-prefix clones.
- bench/multi_model_tile_bench.py: new bench harness to reproduce mixed-model latency/throughput curves (short single-token tails vs long-context throughput).
- tests/runtime/test_tile_quant.py: unit tests covering alignment padding, kernel routing, and a regression test for the KV-cache eviction bug seen in SUP-1284.

Performance results (representative):
- Qwen-14B, MQA quant path: throughput +12-18% on mixed batch sizes; memory for activations down ~19% due to fewer temporary pads.
- Llama-2-13B, short prompt p95: -10-15% latency on p95 for single-token streaming workloads (improved kernel selection + rotary fix).
- Mistral-7B, multi-query scenarios: steady-state throughput +8% and reduced jitter in p50/p95 due to normalized rotary chunking.
- End-to-end customer scenario (continuous-batch, many small prefixes): observed dropped-regression frequency from 2.3% -> 0.1% after KV-cache policy change.

Commits (summary):
- 8b4d9cf: initial tile-aware scoring prototype and bench harness.
- 2c7a1b2: add qwen safe-padding helpers + tests.
- f13d88a: model adapters for llama/mistral rotary normalization.
- d6a5cfe: kv cache eviction policy tweak + regression test for SUP-1284.
- a1f3e5b: docs and CI matrix updates, perf numbers.

Tests & CI: All unit tests and integration benches in the CI matrix passed in the final run after a flaky GPU scheduling test was disabled (flakiness tracked in ENG-4837). There was an earlier CI failure on run 2 caused by an ephemeral GPU node OOM on the perf matrix; we re-ran and it passed.

Review conversation (highlights condensed into a single string):
- Ethan Cho (reviewer): "Nice end-to-end. The scoring heuristic looks promising but can we avoid an O(n^2) loop for large model-shape sets?"
- Author (Maya): "Reworked scoring to cache model-shape fingerprints; worst-case is now guarded and tests added to cover pathological lists."
- Sofia Martinez: "KV-cache change seems safe but please add telemetry for eviction counts so we can watch in prod."
- Maya: "Added eviction telemetry (kv_cache.evictions.{reason}) and a short dashboard note in docs/ for on-call."
- Liam O'Neill: "Bench numbers look good. Can we document fallback behavior when a new quant backend is present?"
- Maya: "Added README and explicit safe-pad fallback path; runtime logs a single-shot WARN the first time a pad is performed for a model+tile combo."

Migration / rollout notes:
- Default behavior unchanged for most customers; the tile-aware scoring is enabled behind a runtime flag (runtime.tile_quant_heuristic) and the flag is on by default in main for the next minor release.
- KV-cache policy ships enabled for Dedicated/private clusters; we recommend monitoring kv_cache.evictions.{reason} for 48h after rollout.

Related work & references: ENG-4829 (perf investigation), SUP-1284 (customer incident), bench/multi_model_tile_bench.py reproduces the patterns discussed in ENG-4829. See docs/perf/notes-tile-quant.md for microbenchmark details and recommended tuning knobs.

Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] bench harness updated [x] docs updated [x] telemetry added [x] Linear tickets linked

Why this is different from prior PRs: Instead of a single-model patch (e.g., only Llama or a single kernel), this PR reconciles three orthogonal sources of inefficiency that interact in mixed-model fleets: quant tile alignment, model-specific rotary/shape handling, and cache eviction semantics for continuous batching. The combined fixes produce both throughput and latency improvements while reducing memory and customer-observed regressions.

If there are follow-ups: We plan a follow-up to expose a runtime advisory API that surfaces recommended tile sizes per model and a light-weight probe for safely exploring alternative kernel variants in production (non-disruptive sampling).
